edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary of $500,000 (the “Base Salary”), payable in accordance with the Company's regular payroll practices, plus benefits under the Company's applicable benefit plans, subject to their terms.

3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive's employment without Cause (other than due to death or disability), or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, the Company shall pay severance equal to two times the Executive's annual Base Salary in effect immediately before termination, disregarding any reduction giving rise to Good Reason. Severance shall be paid in substantially equal installments over 24 months under the Company's regular payroll practices. For the same period, the Company shall continue its employer contributions toward the Executive's and eligible dependents' medical, dental and vision coverage at the levels in effect immediately before termination, subject to timely election of continuation coverage and payment of the employee share. If continued participation is unavailable under applicable law or plan terms, the Company shall provide an economically equivalent taxable payment. Benefit continuation shall cease when the Executive becomes eligible for comparable coverage through another employer. Severance and benefit continuation are conditioned on the Executive signing and not revoking a customary release of employment-related claims in favor of the Company within 60 days after termination. Payments shall begin on the first regular payroll date after that 60-day period, with a catch-up payment for installments otherwise due, subject to any delay required by Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code. Accrued salary, properly reimbursable expenses and vested benefits shall be paid independently of the release requirement.

4. TERMINATION DEFINITIONS. “Cause” means (a) conviction of, or a plea of guilty or no contest to, a felony involving fraud, dishonesty or moral turpitude; (b) fraud, embezzlement or material misappropriation involving the Company; (c) willful misconduct or gross negligence in performing the Executive's duties that materially harms the Company; or (d) a material breach of this Agreement or a willful, continued failure to perform lawful duties reasonably assigned consistent with the Executive's position. For conduct capable of cure under clauses (c) or (d), Cause requires written notice specifying the grounds and failure to cure within 30 days after receipt. “Good Reason” means, without the Executive's written consent, (i) a material reduction in Base Salary; (ii) a material diminution in the Executive's authority, duties or responsibilities; (iii) relocation of the Executive's principal workplace by more than 50 miles that materially increases the Executive's commute; or (iv) the Company's material breach of this Agreement. Good Reason exists only if the Executive gives written notice specifying the condition within 90 days after its initial occurrence, the Company fails to cure within 30 days after receiving notice, and the Executive resigns within 30 days after that cure period expires. No post-employment non-compete restriction applies under this Agreement.
